detail: Read .claude/settings.json: allow has Bash(make:*), Bash(werk:*), Bash(bun src/cli.ts:*); ask has accept/remove/restore for both werk and bun src/cli.ts. A model of Claude Code's deny>ask>allow precedence with a personal allow of werk:*, Bash(*) still gives ask for the three verbs and allow for make lint. Could not run real Claude Code, so this checks the rules, not a live prompt.

Ran src/claude/lint-hook.ts in a temp repo with the repo biome.json: wrong indent + unused import was fixed on disk, exit 0, empty stderr; a missing hook dependency gave exit 2 with useExhaustiveDependencies on stderr and the edit kept; the fixed edit gave exit 0 and empty stderr. Settings wire the hook to Write|Edit|MultiEdit.

Ran src/claude/check-subagent-links.ts against temp roots: all links + a plain dev-only file exits 0; a copy exits 1 naming the subagent as 'not a link'; restored link exits 0; removed link exits 1 naming it 'no link'; dev-only file never named.

Allow list is exactly make, werk, bun src/cli.ts patterns; none is a network or outside-write command by pattern (note: make e2e/install themselves fetch packages, since 'every make target' is allowed). No SKILL.md, .claude/skills, .mcp.json or mcpServers in tracked files/settings. In a temp git repo with the repo .gitignore, .claude/settings.local.json is absent from git status.
Ran bun src/release/build.ts into a temp dir: exit 0, four executables (darwin-arm64/x64, linux-arm64/x64), each with a .sha256 whose digest equals sha256 of the file.

Copied the darwin-arm64 executable alone into an empty git folder, PATH=/usr/bin:/bin (no bun), started 'serve'; it printed 'serving on http://127.0.0.1:PORT'; Chromium loaded / and showed #screen with no 4xx/5xx responses. Only a .werk folder (serve.lock, fold-ms.jsonl, the project's map state) appeared next to it; no client or program files.

Executable 'help' output is byte-identical to 'bun src/cli.ts help' from the checkout, non-empty, >10 verbs. 'add one --title One' then 'show one' ran through the executable with exit 0 and no missing-file error.

Started the executable in an empty project, sent a chat message in Chromium with the fake agent as chat role. The recorded launch's --append-system-prompt names the command as "<exe path>" add ... and contains no 'cli.ts' and no 'bun'. The fake agent cannot run the command itself, so I ran the named executable 'help' myself: exit 0.

Parsed ci.yml (Bun.YAML): push on main; steps in order make lint, typecheck, test, test-coverage, e2e, smoke, none continue-on-error, no cache. make -n lint on a tree with no node_modules shows 'bun install --frozen-lockfile' before the lint. smoke script builds --current and starts it and reads the map. A real GitHub run and the 'able to be released' mark were not exercised.

ci.yml has a pull_request trigger and one job, so a PR gets the same steps incl. make smoke (checked). The 'merge button only on green' part is a GitHub branch-protection setting that is not in the repository and cannot be tested locally.

Each check is its own step so a red run names the failed step, and the workflow has no revert/undo (checked). 'Commit cannot be released' and 'failure as basis for a follow-up ticket' need GitHub run status and a consumer of it; the repo has no code for either, and I could not run GitHub.

.bun-version holds one exact x.y.z; oven-sh/setup-bun with bun-version-file: .bun-version is a step before every run step, with no literal bun-version override. The run log of a real GitHub run was not read.

Ran src/release/smoke.ts on a stand-in executable that prints 'serving on ...' but answers every request 500: exits non-zero and says the read answered 500. In ci.yml make smoke is the last step, so the run ends red.
